faqs.a: Fast fashion is cheap, trendy clothing produced quickly and in large volumes so that shoppers can keep buying the latest styles. The clothes are often low in quality and wear out after a few washes, which creates a cycle of buying, throwing away and buying again.

faqs.q: Why is fast fashion bad for the environment?
faqs.a: Because clothes are made cheaply and discarded quickly, huge amounts of textile waste end up in landfills. Synthetic fabrics also shed microplastic fibres when washed, and producing so many garments uses large amounts of water, energy and chemical dyes.

faqs.q: Can cheap clothes cause skin problems?
faqs.a: They can for some people. Low-cost fabrics and dyes may contain chemicals that irritate sensitive skin or trigger allergic reactions. Washing new clothes before you wear them can help, and if you get a rash that does not settle or keeps coming back, see a doctor or dermatologist.

faqs.q: How can I avoid fast fashion on a budget?
faqs.a: Buy fewer but better-made pieces in timeless styles, shop at thrift and second-hand stores, swap clothes with friends and repair or restyle what you already own. Washing clothes less often and in cold water also helps them last longer, which saves money over time.
